cards.text: This is a psalm of Asaph, chief of the worship leaders King David appointed (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). It opens with God presiding in the divine assembly. Friend, the most serious meeting in my bakery is me versus me deciding chips or sprinkles, but THIS is a meeting.

cards.question: God presides in the divine assembly. There, He renders ___

cards.text: Then God speaks, and He opens with a question. You ever get called into a meeting and the boss starts with "How long are we gonna keep doing this?" NOBODY in that room is relaxed.

cards.question: In the divine assembly, God asks how long they'll keep doing something. What is it?

answers.text: Judging unjustly and favoring the wicked
Ignoring the feasts and the sacrifices
Refusing to hear any cases at all

cards.text: So what SHOULD they be doing? God LAYS. IT. OUT: uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed, and He's just getting started.

cards.question: God tells the assembly whose cause to defend. Whose is it?
God tells the assembly to rescue the weak and needy and save them from the hand of the wicked.

cards.text: Then comes a heavy line. They don't know, they don't understand, and they wander in the darkness. I know dark, friend. I did YEARS in the back of a junk drawer. Zero stars.

cards.question: Right after the line about wandering in the darkness, the psalm says all the foundations of the earth are ___

cards.text: Now God reminds them of something He has said about them. Friend, when the One who made everything quotes Himself, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: God reminds the ones He's judging what He has said they are. What is it?

answers.text: Gods and sons of the Most High
Priests and servants of the temple

cards.text: Then comes one little word: But. You ever hear "You're doing great, but"? Friend, everything before that but just packed up and left the building.

cards.question: Big title and all, what does God say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will be scattered among the nations
They will be turned into servants

cards.question: God also tells them that like rulers they will fall.

cards.text: Then the psalm turns. It stops reporting on the assembly and calls out to God Himself to arise.

cards.question: The psalm asks God to arise and judge only the nation of Israel.
The psalm calls on God to judge the earth. What reason does it give?

answers.text: All the nations are His inheritance
The rulers have all stepped down
The nations have asked Him to

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 mentions chips, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank finishes the exact line 'He renders ___' from verse 1. No earlier card sets up what God does in the assembly, so the baker is completing wording they haven't seen. The card doesn't test a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to finish the line 'all the foundations of the earth are ___' from verse 5. Card 8 tells nothing about the earth or its foundations, so this is guessing the next words of a poetic line. It doesn't ask about the movement or the meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Card 5 has just said God wants them to uphold the rights of the afflicted and oppressed. That setup rules out the wrong answer 'The strong and the wealthy', which is also a plain opposite of the right answer and doesn't sound like a believable pick.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question 'Big title and all, what does God say will happen to them?' points back to card 11 with 'Big title' and 'them'. Card 11 is no longer on screen, and the question never says who 'them' is: the ones God called gods and sons of the Most High.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'God also tells them that like rulers they will fall.' leans on the card before it for who 'them' is and what 'also' adds to. It never says it's the ones God called gods.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: In verse 5 the core action is not knowing or understanding and wandering in darkness. The comparison is Papa Dorin lying stuck in a literal dark drawer, which isn't the same action, since he wasn't wandering or failing to understand. The 'Zero stars' review gag also adds a second image.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
